findings.text: World switch restore entry for user thread identity and for EL1 system state. User handling covers only TPIDR_EL0 and TPIDRRO_EL0. EL1 handling covers identity, memory, fault, timer and address controls plus optional extensions from the per vCPU context.

EL1 restore programs VPIDR_EL2 and VMPIDR_EL2 first from supplied identity values. When VHE is present or the speculative translation workaround is absent, SCTLR and TCR are restored together early. When non VHE with the workaround, guest contexts get TCR with table walk disables plus a barrier, while host running contexts get SCTLR then TCR late after a barrier once stage two is off. A running flag in the context distinguishes host from guest.

Optional EL1 state is gated. TCR2 is handled only when TCRX support is present. PIR and PIRE0 additionally require PIE support. POR additionally requires POE support. TFSR and TFSRE0 require MTE support. The SCTLR2 register requires SCTLR2 capability. NVHCR is programmed only for nested NV3 contexts.

Presence helpers combine a host capability with a per VM option. PIE, TCRX, POE and SCTLR2 helpers return false when the corresponding host capability is absent, otherwise they consult the owning VM through a hyp address translation. The MTE helper consults only the per VM flag without an explicit host capability check in the fragment.

Thirty two bit restore is a no op unless the vCPU runs thirty two bit at EL1. Otherwise it restores banked saved status for abort, undefined, irq and fiq plus DACR32_EL2 and IFSR32_EL2. DBGVCR32_EL2 additionally requires VHE or debug registers in use.

Virtual EL2 restore maps saved EL2 named state onto the EL1 system interface. Common PAR_EL1 and TPIDR_EL1 plus identity from MIDR and MPIDR and base memory views for MAIR, VBAR, CONTEXTIDR and AMAIR are always programmed. When E2H is set, control, access, translation and timer views are copied directly. When E2H is clear, control, access and translation views go through translation helpers and the timer view is omitted as it only affects non VHE EL1.

Virtual EL2 tail handles extensions and fault return state. TCR2 is handled only with TCRX support, with PIR and PIRE0 further gated by PIE and POR further gated by POE. Fault, address, stack and return state are always programmed, while the SCTLR2 register is programmed only with SCTLR2 capability.
MPAM guest load is a no op unless MPAM is supported. Otherwise it preserves partition and monitor fields from MPAM0_EL1 while asserting the enable control in MPAM1.

Hardware MMU selection entry for vCPU load. Hyp contexts reuse the primary VM MMU when unassigned. Nested contexts allocate under lock when unassigned and request L1 VNCR mapping when the NV control flag is set in HCR.

Nested stage two context moves between unassigned, assigned and pending unmap. Load assigns when empty. Lookup hit reuses. Lookup miss scans the pool and snapshots keys. Recycled valid entries are marked pending and a nested unmap request ensures they are fully unmapped before any vCPU uses them, with multiple vCPUs allowed to help.

Nested S2 lookup and allocation require write hold on the VM MMU lock, with an assertion in both paths. The vCPU load path takes a write scoped guard only when a nested assignment is missing, avoiding lock traffic on the reuse fast path.

Lookup ignores the CnP bit in VTTBR. Enabled guests match only entries that are enabled with equal full VTTBR and equal VTCR. Disabled guests match only entries that are disabled with equal VMID portion, since translation disabled tables remain tagged by VMID.

Allocation scans the fixed pool round robin from a next cursor and picks the first entry with zero reference count, then advances the cursor. It retires a still valid entry by removing its debug view and marking pending unmap. It snapshots VTTBR without CnP plus VTCR plus the HCR enable flag, creates a debug view, bumps the reference count and raises an unmap request when pending.

Allocation assumes a spare context exists and fails hard when the scan finds no zero count entry. A recycled entry must not be used until its pending unmap completes, enforced by raising the unmap request even when the pending flag was set by another vCPU.

Second stage MMU record holds tlb_vttbr and tlb_vtcr as TLB keys plus nested_stage2_enabled and pending_unmap flags plus refcnt and shadow_pt_debugfs_dentry and an arch back pointer. VM arch holds nested_mmus with nested_mmus_size and nested_mmus_next cursor.

Nested debug file name encodes VTTBR and VTCR in hex plus an enabled or disabled word. Creation registers a read only file under the nested debug directory and stores the returned dentry in the MMU record. Removal deletes that stored dentry.

PMU guest restore entry swaps EL0 counting between guest and host. It does nothing without PMU version three support or without VHE. Otherwise it disables preemption, fetches per CPU guest and host masks, enables guest events and disables host events, then re enables preemption.

Event type access dispatches by counter identity. The cycle counter uses the cycle filter accessor and the instruction counter uses the instruction filter accessor, while other counters use the indexed general accessor. Enabling clears the EL0 exclusion control and disabling sets it, iterating over set bits up to the hardware event limit.
PMU event record holds events_guest and events_host masks. It is accessed per CPU through the CPU local pointer for the global event structure.

VGIC load entry selects version handling. When the interrupt controller is not in kernel or not initialized, it only activates GICv3 traps on VHE with CPU interface present and returns. Otherwise it dispatches by model to KVM_DEV_TYPE_ARM_VGIC_V5 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_ARM_VGIC_V3 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_ARM_VGIC_V2 handling, with version two choosing version three handling when the CPU interface is present. Unknown models fail hard.

GICv3 trap activation orders SRE, VMCR and HCR programming. Disabled virtualization with HCR enable clear forces SRE on with a barrier. Enabled compat with SRE clear programs SRE off, then VMCR, with extra barriers on VHE. V2 compatibility clears the SRE enable control. HCR trap controls plus enable are written when trap static control is set or ITS virtualization is present or compat mode is active.

APR restore size derives from the virtualization trap register. A patched accessor reads the register, preemption bit count is the encoded field plus one, and one, two or four words per priority group are written with fallthrough at the six and seven thresholds, separately for group zero and group one.
List register file holds sixteen entries selected by low four bits of the index. Active priority state holds up to four words per group.
Nested VGIC state is possible only in nested contexts. The check looks at HCR_IMO and HCR_FMO, warns once on asymmetric settings and reports nested when either override is set.

GICv3 load has nested and flat paths. Nested path asserts nested state, builds shadow state, restores VMCR and APRs, activates traps, programs each used list register and propagates the used count to the vCPU record. Flat path restores via hypercall unless protected, activates traps on VHE, then loads V4 state with a warning on failure.

V3 CPU interface holds vgic_hcr and vgic_sre and vgic_vmcr plus vgic_ap0r and vgic_ap1r arrays plus vgic_lr array with used_lrs count plus an ITS association. V2 CPU interface holds vgic_vmcr and vgic_apr. Nested shadow holds a separate V3 copy whose used count is copied back.

VMCR and APR restore orders compat mode before state. Compat enable does nothing without GICv5 CPU interface, otherwise it sets V3 mode with a barrier and wait. VMCR is written only when the SRE flag is set, while APR restore always runs.
GICv2 load programs VMCR and APR through relaxed writes to the virtual control base.
Exposes hardware MMU loader with S2 lookup helper and nested debug create and remove helpers for use by vCPU load and nested management paths.
Exposes PMU guest restore entry with per CPU event accessor for world switch use.
Exposes top level VGIC load dispatcher with version specific loaders and nested state query and nested loader.
Hyp local restore helpers for user, EL1, thirty two bit, virtual EL2, MPAM and GIC state are available to world switch paths.
PMU restore holds preemption disabled while fetching per CPU masks and updating event filters, keeping CPU local state stable across the swap.
Unknown VGIC models fail hard. Nested loader asserts nested state. Asymmetric interrupt override warns once. V4 load failure warns but does not abort the vCPU load in the fragment.
Nested S2 debug file is created with owner read only permission.
Trap control and trap register accessors use runtime patched sequences returning only low bits. HCR trap bits come from the low sixteen bits path and VTR comes from the low thirty two bits path.
